PC: CAB assessment: check carotid pulse, look for respiratory effort
Request cardiac monitor and pulse ox, check blood pressure
Provide supplemental oxygen (nonrebreather will take pulse ox up to 98% over one minute, nasal cannula will have no effect)
Assess level of consciousness and pupils (GCS = 3, anisocoric)
Check finger stick blood glucose (nurse will report that it is 38)
Administer D-50 (will cause patient to moan and open eyes, but no speech or commands; repeat FSBG if requested will be 128)
Reassess level of consciousness and pupils (GCS now 8 – eyes open to pain (2), moans (2), withdraws to pain (4), patient remains anisocoric)
MK: Consider naloxone (defined as asking about opiate use, discussing whether it would be appropriate with nurse, etc – NOT required to “order” it, as learners would not be ordering meds at this stage – any discussion of opiates or naloxone will prompt nurse to give a 0.4mg dose “per hospital protocol” – this will have no effect)
SBP: Call for help – learners may request either code team or their own resident/attending
